To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the first committed step of heme biosynthetic pathway in S. typhumurium is controlled by a posttranscriptionally mediated increase in the abundance (amount) of the enzyme glutamyt-RNA reductase (encoded by hemA) during heme limitation.
the activity and abundance of glutamyl tRNA reductase are increased in cells of Salmonella and Escherichium that are heme limited.

the first committed enzyme in the biosynthetic pathway for heme is induced by heme limitation in Salmonella typhilumurium and that the induction is due to a posttranscription increase in the abundance and stability of the HemA polypeptide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of heme biosynthetic enzymes in Salmonella typhi-murium.
the regulation of heme biosynthetic enzymes in Salmonella typhi- murium and the mechanisms involved in the regulation of hemesynthetic enzymes in S. typhimu- rium.
the regulation of the first committed step of heme biosynthetic pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
heme limitation results in a significant increase in glutamyl-tRNareductase (HmA) activity by an induction of the protein.
the regulation of HemA is mediated by a posttranscriptionally induced increase in protein abundance during heme limitation.

HemA enzyme activity is greatly elevated during growth of Salmonella typhmurium in the absence of exogenous heme, and that this regulation occurs through an increase in the amount of HemA protein, which may result from either an increase in HemA protein stability or an increase in hemA gene transcription.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
heme limitation results in an increase in glutamyl-tRNAREductase (Hema) enzyme activity and protein abundance.
heme limitation results in increased HemA protein levels through a mechanism that is not mediated at the level of transcription of hemA.
the activity of glutamyal-tRNA reductases in heme-limtited Salmonella and Escherichria coli is greatly elevated through a mechanism which increases the abundance of the protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the abundance of glutamyl tRNA reductase is greatly elevated during periods of heme limitation.

the regulation of heme biosynthetic enzyme activity in S. typhmurium is mediated by an induction in the level of the enzyme protein, rather than by an increase in enzyme activity due to an increase in enzyme concentration, as has been observed for some other bacterial enzymes.
the abundance of the glutamyl-tRNareductase (HmA) enzyme is increased during heme limitation.
